sections.label: Wage growth and income inequality
sections.summary: Median income of resident workers rose 3.4% above inflation, and income inequality after taxes and transfers is at its lowest since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Singaporeans saw wage increases that outpaced inflation – the median income of resident workers rose by 3.4% above inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Income inequality, after government taxes and transfers, is at its lowest since 2000.

sections.label: Growth and inflation projections
sections.summary: Growth is projected at 1% to 3%, while inflation is expected to average 1.5% to 2.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Growth is projected at 1% to 3%, while inflation is expected to average 1.5% to 2.5%.

sections.label: Assurance Package enhancement
sections.summary: Last year, the Assurance Package was enhanced by $1.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Last year, I enhanced the Assurance Package by $1.9 billion.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers for households
sections.summary: $800 in Community Development Council Vouchers will be provided to every Singaporean household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, I will provide $800 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers to every Singaporean household.

sections.label: Support for HDB households
sections.summary: Eligible Housing and Development Board households will receive up to $760 this financial year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Eligible Housing and Development Board (HDB) households will receive up to $760 this financial year.

sections.label: Support for families with children
sections.summary: Families will receive $500 in LifeSG credits for each Singaporean child aged 12 and below this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Third, I will provide more support to families with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They will receive $500 in LifeSG credits for each Singaporean child aged 12 and below this year.

sections.label: Edusave top-up for youths
sections.summary: Singaporeans aged 13 to 20 this year each receive a $500 top-up to their Edusave or Post-Secondary Education Account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Every Singaporean aged 13 to 20 this year will also receive a $500 top-up to their Edusave account, or their Post-Secondary Education Account.

sections.label: Long-Term Assistance and Singapore Allowance
sections.summary: A one-person Long-Term Assistance household gets $120 more monthly, taking cash assistance to $760, and the Singapore Allowance rises from $350 to $390 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, a one-person household on Long-Term Assistance will receive an additional $120 each month, bringing the monthly cash assistance to $760.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In tandem, we will increase the Singapore Allowance, which is an ex-gratia payment that some of our pensioners receive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It will increase from $350 to $390 each month, to support those with smaller pensions.

sections.label: Corporate Income Tax rebate
sections.summary: A 50% Corporate Income Tax rebate is introduced in the Year of Assessment 2025, as businesses face higher rent and labour costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Higher prices also affect our businesses, many of whom are grappling with the higher costs of rent and labour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I will introduce a 50% Corporate Income Tax rebate in the Year of Assessment 2025.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme enhancement
sections.summary: Government co-funding levels for wage increases rise from 30% in 2025 to 40%, and from 15% in 2026 to 20%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government will continue to share this responsibility with employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And taking into account feedback from employers, I will enhance the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, by increasing the Government’s co-funding levels for wage increases from 30% in 2025 to 40%, and from 15% in 2026 to 20%.

sections.label: Budget's three key areas
sections.summary: The Budget emphasises three key areas: technology and innovation, the enterprise ecosystem, and infrastructure investments amidst resource constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To take our economy forward, this Budget will emphasise three key areas: technology and innovation, our enterprise ecosystem, as well as our infrastructure investments amidst resource constraints.

sections.label: Singapore's semi-conductor strengths
sections.summary: Singapore supplies more than 10% of chips and produces one-fifth of semi-conductor equipment worldwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We also have considerable strengths in several industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are a key player in semi-conductors, supplying more than 10% of chips and producing one-fifth of semi-conductor equipment worldwide.

sections.label: Singapore DNA chips and pharma
sections.summary: Singapore produces over 80% of the world's DNA chips and hosts eight of the top 10 pharmaceutical companies' manufacturing operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Singapore alone produces more than 80% of the world’s DNA chips.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Eight of the world’s top 10 pharmaceutical companies have manufacturing operations here.

sections.label: National Productivity Fund top-up
sections.summary: The National Productivity Fund will be topped up by $3 billion to maximise competitive strengths, as major economies cannot be outbid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We cannot afford to outbid the major economies, but we do need to set aside sufficient resources to maximise our competitive strengths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I will top up the National Productivity Fund by $3 billion.

sections.label: National semiconductor R&D fabrication facility
sections.summary: A new national semiconductor R&D fabrication facility will be developed in the semi-conductor space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the semi-conductor space, we will develop a new national semiconductor R&D fabrication facility.

sections.label: EDB Global Founder Programme
sections.summary: EDB will launch a Global Founder Programme later this year to encourage global founders to anchor and grow new ventures in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As our investment promotion agency, the Economic Development Board (EDB), has close links with these multinational firms and entrepreneurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, EDB will launch a Global Founder Programme later this year to encourage global founders to anchor and grow more new ventures in Singapore.

sections.label: Enterprise Compute Initiative funding
sections.summary: Up to $150 million will be set aside for a new Enterprise Compute Initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To support this, I will set aside up to $150 million for a new Enterprise Compute Initiative.

sections.label: Enterprise growth investment funds
sections.summary: Over the past five years, over $1.8 billion was set aside to support enterprise growth through investment funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the past five years, we have set aside over $1.8 billion to support enterprise growth through investment funds.

sections.label: New Private Credit Growth Fund
sections.summary: A new $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund will be introduced, as few private credit funds focus on Asia or Singapore-based enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But few of these private credit funds focus on Asia, much less Singapore-based enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we will introduce a new $1 billion Private Credit Growth Fund.

sections.label: Tax incentives for Singapore listings
sections.summary: Tax-related recommendations were submitted to MOF for the Budget, and tax incentives will be introduced for Singapore-based companies and fund managers that list in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They include several tax-related recommendations which have been submitted to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), just in time for the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I accept their recommendations and will introduce tax incentives for Singapore-based companies and fund managers that choose to list in Singapore and grow their economic activities here.

sections.label: Changi Airport Development Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Changi Airport Development Fund will be topped up by $5 billion, and the Government will provide a guarantee to Changi Airport Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To ensure sufficient resources to develop our air hub, I will top up the Changi Airport Development Fund by $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: With the President’s concurrence, the Government will also provide a guarantee to Changi Airport Group.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This will help to lower the cost of borrowings needed to develop Terminal 5 and supporting infrastructure in Changi East.

sections.label: Electricity imports by 2035
sections.summary: By 2035, about one-third of projected electricity demand is expected to be met through electricity imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: By 2035, we expect that about one-third of our projected electricity demand can be met through electricity imports.

sections.label: Studying nuclear energy deployment
sections.summary: Singapore will study potential nuclear energy deployment and build capabilities, with agreements signed with the US on civil nuclear cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Malaysia and Indonesia also have experience in nuclear technologies and have operated research reactors for some time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will therefore study the potential deployment of nuclear energy in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will take further steps to systematically build up our capabilities in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have signed agreements with the US on civil nuclear cooperation.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Future Energy Fund, established last year, will be topped up by $5 billion to support securing clean power for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is why we established the Future Energy Fund last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will top up the Fund by $5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This will further support our critical undertaking to secure clean power for Singapore.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme gives Singaporeans aged 40 and above $4,000 in SkillsFuture Credit and a training allowance of up to $3,000 monthly for selected full-time courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At last year’s Budget, I introduced the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to support mid-career Singaporeans in getting a significant skills reboot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under the programme, all Singaporeans aged 40 years and above will get $4,000 in SkillsFuture Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: From next month, individuals can apply for a training allowance of up to $3,000 per month for selected full-time courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They will have 24 months’ worth of allowance, which is up to $72,000 per worker.

sections.label: Part-time training allowance
sections.summary: The training allowance is extended to workers undergoing part-time training, who can receive a fixed $300 per month to defray learning expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: While workers like Zarina continue to earn their salaries during part-time training, they also incur training-related expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will therefore extend the training allowance to workers undergoing part-time training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They can enjoy a fixed allowance of $300 per month to defray their learning expenses.

sections.label: Existing credit expiry extended
sections.summary: Companies can continue to use the existing credit, which was due to expire in June this year but will be extended until the new credit is ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Meanwhile, companies can continue to use the existing credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It was originally due to expire in June this year, but we will extend it until the new credit is ready.

sections.label: NTUC CTC grant funding
sections.summary: Additional funding of around $200 million is set aside for NTUC's CTC grant, which will also be expanded to support employer-led training leading to formal qualifications or certifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: NTUC would like to start more CTCs and help more companies transform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will set aside additional funding of around $200 million for NTUC’s CTC grant, to help more companies transform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also expand the CTC grant to support employer-led training that leads to formal qualifications or certifications.

sections.label: Financial support for workers
sections.summary: The scheme will provide financial support of up to $6,000 over six months to give workers assurance during training or job search.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The scheme will provide financial support of up to $6,000 over six months, to give our workers assurance as they undergo training or search for jobs.

sections.label: Senior Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Senior Employment Credit is extended by one year to end-2026, and the qualifying age for the highest SEC wage support tier is raised to 69 from 68.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the immediate term, I will extend the Senior Employment Credit (SEC) by one year to end-2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In line with the increase in the re-employment age, I will raise the qualifying age for the highest SEC wage support tier to 69 years old, from 68 years old today.

sections.label: CPF rates for senior workers
sections.summary: CPF contribution rates for those aged above 55 to 65 will rise 1.5 percentage points in 2026, with a CPF Transition Offset for employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In line with the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Older Workers, we will proceed with the next step of planned Central Provident Fund (CPF) contribution rate increases for senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will increase the CPF contribution rates for those aged above 55 to 65 by 1.5 percentage points in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also continue to provide the CPF Transition Offset to employers for another year to cover half of the increase in employer contributions for 2026.

sections.label: Uplifting Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Uplifting Employment Credit will be extended to end-2028 to encourage more employers to hire ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To encourage more employers to hire ex-offenders, I will extend the Uplifting Employment Credit to end-2028.

sections.label: New climate target submission
sections.summary: A new climate target was submitted to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, committing to emissions of 45 to 50 million tonnes by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Just a week ago, we submitted our new climate target to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We have committed to reducing our emissions to between 45 and 50 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2035.

sections.label: Annual fees for electric vehicles
sections.summary: The AFC will be $250 per year for electric heavy goods vehicles, and $190 and $550 per year for electric minibuses and large buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The AFC will be set at $250 per year for electric heavy goods vehicles, and $190 and $550 per year for electric minibuses and large buses respectively.

sections.label: Rail network expansion target
sections.summary: The target is for eight in 10 households to be within a 10-minute walk from a train station, with over $60 billion invested this decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our target is for eight in 10 households to be within a 10-minute walk from a train station.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are investing over $60 billion in this decade to expand and renew our rail network, which forms the backbone of our public transport system.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund top-up
sections.summary: The Coastal and Flood Protection Fund will be topped up by $5 billion to proceed with major investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But it would be prudent to set aside funds now to ensure we can proceed with these major investments, which will benefit current and future generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, I will top up the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund by $5 billion.

sections.label: Climate Vouchers for households
sections.summary: The Climate Friendly Households Programme is enhanced with an extra $100 in Climate Vouchers for HDB households and extended to citizen households in private properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Last year, we enhanced the Climate Friendly Households Programme by extending it to all HDB households, increased the vouchers quantum to $300 and expanded its use to a broader range of energy- and water-efficient products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will further enhance the programme by providing an additional $100 worth of Climate Vouchers to HDB households.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also extend the Climate Vouchers to all Singapore Citizen households living in private properties.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for families
sections.summary: Families can receive up to $30,000 in CPF top-ups if the adults sustain employment and save up for a home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, families can receive up to $30,000 in CPF top-ups if the adults sustain employment and do their part to save up for a home.

sections.label: Grant for smaller flats
sections.summary: Eligible families can receive a $50,000 grant to buy a new 2-room Flexi or Standard 3-room flat on a shorter lease.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Today, eligible families can receive a $50,000 grant to buy a new 2-room Flexi or Standard 3-room flat on a shorter lease.

sections.label: Caps on centre fees
sections.summary: Fees will be capped at $610 for Anchor Operator centres and $650 for Partner Operator centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The fees will be capped at $610 for Anchor Operator centres and $650 for Partner Operator centres.

sections.label: Large Families Scheme support
sections.summary: A Large Families Scheme will support married couples with or aspiring to three or more children, starting with a $5,000 increase in the Child Development Account First Step Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Couples with more children often worry about additional costs, because the demands grow with each additional child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will introduce a Large Families Scheme to support married couples who have, or aspire to have, three or more children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, a $5,000 increase in the Child Development Account First Step Grant.

sections.label: Large Family MediSave Grant
sections.summary: A new $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant is introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, a new $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant.

sections.label: LifeSG credits for third children
sections.summary: Families receive $1,000 in LifeSG credits annually for each third and subsequent child, in the years the child turns one to six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Third, $1,000 in LifeSG credits will be disbursed annually to families for each of their third and subsequent children, during the years that the child turns one to six.

sections.label: Five-year Matched MediSave Scheme
sections.summary: A five-year Matched MediSave Scheme will be introduced to provide more assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To provide more assurance, we will introduce a five-year Matched MediSave Scheme.

sections.label: Subsidies for residential long-term care
sections.summary: Existing subsidies for residential long-term care services will increase by up to 15 percentage points for seniors with more severe care needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will increase our support for seniors with more severe care needs and who may require residential care, such as in a nursing home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will increase existing subsidies for residential long-term care services by up to 15 percentage points.

sections.label: Enhanced Home Caregiving Grant support
sections.summary: The maximum grant rises to $600 monthly and qualifying per capita household income to $4,800, benefiting at least 80,000 seniors from next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The maximum grant will increase to $600 per month, from $400 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also raise the maximum qualifying per capita household income for the Home Caregiving Grant to $4,800, so that more caregivers receive support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We expect at least 80,000 seniors to benefit from the enhanced long-term care subsidies and grants, which will be implemented from next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The enhancements are expected to cost around $300 million in FY2026, and more in future years, as our population continues to age.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit extension
sections.summary: The Enabling Employment Credit will be extended to end-2028 to offset wages for persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In particular, we will extend the Enabling Employment Credit to end-2028, to offset wages for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Matching grant for caregiver top-ups
sections.summary: A dollar-for-dollar matching grant will be provided for top-ups by lower- and middle-income caregivers to trust accounts, up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To support these efforts, we will provide a dollar-for-dollar matching grant for top-ups by lower- and middle-income caregivers to the trust accounts, up to $10,000.

sections.label: Personal Income Tax Rebate 2025
sections.summary: A 60% Personal Income Tax Rebate for Year of Assessment 2025, capped at $200, mostly benefiting middle-income workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, I will provide a Personal Income Tax Rebate of 60%, for the Year of Assessment 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This will be capped at $200, so that the rebate mostly benefits our middle-income workers.

sections.label: Credits for Singaporeans aged 18
sections.summary: All Singaporeans aged 18 and above this year receive $100 in credits for eligible activities like arts, museum and heritage experiences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: All Singaporeans aged 18 and above this year will receive $100 worth of credits, which they can use for eligible activities, like arts and cultural performances, museum exhibitions and heritage experiences.

sections.label: Hawker stall rental support and upgrading
sections.summary: Each stall in centres managed by Government and Government-appointed operators gets one-time $600 rental support, plus up to $1 billion to upgrade and build centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To appreciate our hawkers and market stallholders, we will give each stall in centres managed by Government and Government-appointed operators a one-time rental support of $600 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also allocate up to $1 billion over the next 20 to 30 years to upgrade ageing hawker centres and to build new centres.

sections.label: Cultural Matching Fund top-up extension
sections.summary: A $100 million top-up to the Cultural Matching Fund, extended five years until the end of FY2029, to support charities and social causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This year, we will increase our support for the fund-raising efforts of charities and social causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will provide a $100 million top-up to the Cultural Matching Fund and extend it for five years until the end of FY2029.

sections.label: SG Gives matching grant for donations
sections.summary: A $250 million SG Gives matching grant provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations made through the Community Chest, Collective for a Stronger Society and President's Challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Community Chest, the Collective for a Stronger Society and the President’s Challenge provide platforms that help donors contribute to a range of programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will introduce a $250 million SG Gives matching grant to provide dollar-for-dollar matching for donations made through these platforms.

sections.label: GST rate increase revenues
sections.summary: The Goods and Services Tax rate increase ensures revenues to look after a growing number of seniors, even with rising healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate increase ensures we have the revenues to look after our growing number of seniors, even with rising healthcare costs.

sections.label: Property tax rebate 2025
sections.summary: A rebate of up to 20% for owner-occupied residential properties in 2025 was announced, capped at $1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In November last year, we announced another rebate of up to 20% for owner-occupied residential properties in 2025, capped at $1,000.

sections.label: Corporate Income Tax collections rise
sections.summary: Corporate Income Tax collections, previously about 3.2% of GDP, rose and are projected to reach 4.1% of GDP in FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the past, our Corporate Income Tax collections were quite stable, at about 3.2% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But collections increased significantly in the last two years and are projected to reach 4.1% of GDP in FY2024, which is quite significant.

sections.label: FY2024 and FY2025 surpluses
sections.summary: FY2024 is expected to end with a $6.4 billion surplus, and FY2025 with a similar $6.8 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Overall, I expect to end FY2024 with a surplus of $6.4 billion, or 0.9% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For FY2025, I expect a similar fiscal position, with a surplus of $6.8 billion, or 0.9% of GDP.

sections.label: Domestic Top-up Tax revenue
sections.summary: It is too early to tell if higher Corporate Income Tax collections are temporary, with possible extra revenue from FY2027 under the Domestic Top-up Tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At this juncture, it is too early to determine if the recent increase in Corporate Income Tax collections is temporary or a lasting trend.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There could be some additional Corporate Income Tax revenue from FY2027 onwards, with the implementation of the Domestic Top-up Tax, which will raise the large MNEs’ effective tax rate to 15%.

sections.label: Responsible spending and fiscal upsides
sections.summary: The government will spend responsibly and use near-term fiscal upsides for social and economic needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the meantime, we will spend responsibly and ensure resources are allocated effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If and when there are near-term fiscal upsides, we will put the resources to good use, including for our social and economic needs.

sections.label: Budget 2025 future plans
sections.summary: Budget 2025 sets out plans tackling immediate challenges and laying groundwork for a stronger tomorrow, shaped with all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Budget 2025 sets out clear plans for us to continue this journey with confidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is a Budget for the future – tackling immediate challenges, while laying the groundwork for a stronger, more resilient tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Every Singaporean is supported from birth to old age, with more support given to those with less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Importantly, this is a Budget shaped together with all Singaporeans – advancing our Forward Singapore efforts to build the Singapore we want and empowering each of us to contribute towards our shared future.

sections.label: Financial policy debate adjourned
sections.summary: The debate on approving the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 now stands adjourned under Standing Order No 89.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the Financial Year 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
